overall: The AG found that a Councilor's email to a quorum of the Council was impermissible deliberation, rejected the attorney-client privilege defense, declined uncharged issues, and ordered the email released within 30 days.

allegations.summary: A Councilor emailed eight other Council members about a complaint and how minutes should be handled, allegedly deliberating outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Here, we find that Councilor Matheson engaged in impermissible deliberation outside of a public meeting when he sent the September 13, 2018, email to eight other members of the Council, thereby reaching more than a quorum of the Council.

allegations.summary: The Council argued the email was exempt under attorney-client privilege; the AG rejected this as no basis for keeping a quorum communication private.
allegations.key_passage: However, there is no attorney-client privilege exception to the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Allegations raised only in the complainant's request for further review were not examined because the AG reviews only allegations in the original complaint.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review any allegations made in the request for further review.

remedy: We order the Council’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
We also order that the Council release to the public, within 30 days following its receipt of this determination, the September 13, 2018, email referenced in this letter.
remedy_passage: We also order that the Council release to the public, within 30 days following its receipt of this determination, the September 13, 2018, email referenced in this letter.
